text:
Maia: Quick sync — we need to settle the abstraction for cross-mode fallbacks and failure semantics between Hosted / Dedicated / Private. Not just API shape: who owns state, caching, secrets, routing decisions?
Jordan: Strong +1. We should separate the control-plane contract from runtime responsibilities. E.g., cache ownership, KV eviction, and prefix caching need explicit ownership flags.
Nate: Edge-case: a Private customer might want platform autoscaling signals but cannot expose control-plane endpoints. How do we support that? webhooks? polling?
Sam: Suggest a minimal manifest + optional extensions. Example snippet for the manifest we could standardize on:
```
model: "redwood/gpt-x"
control_role: "orchestrator" # orchestrator | passive | none
cache_ownership: "platform" # platform | customer | hybrid
fallback_policy: ["dedicated", "hosted"]
telemetry_mode: "push" # push | pull | none
kms: {type: "hsm-local", fingerprint: "..."} # fingerprint only in control plane
```
Carla: Important — network/egress constraints. Some regulated customers deny any outbound egress. We must define an "offline-mode" contract: what features are disabled and what local telemetry shim looks like.
Maia: Right. Offline-mode must be explicit in manifest and documented with SLO implications. For example: no function-calling to external tools, no model updates, limited evals.
infra-bot: incident: staging-2 detected blocked egress to control-plane at 2026-03-04T09:12Z — auto-fallback to local cache enabled.
Jordan: Also need unified metrics/trace schema. If Hosted and Private report different metric names, Console won't be able to compare latency/cost across deployments. Suggest enforced metric tags + shim on the agent to translate.
Nate: Security note: when KMS/HSM is local, the control plane should only store key fingerprints and policy envelopes. Never raw material. For Dedicated we allow sealed-transit to platform KMS if customer opts in.
Sam: Tradeoff: thin agent vs heavy runtime. Thin agent keeps logic centralized (easier to patch) but forces more control-plane traffic and higher latency for private setups. Heavy runtime duplicates logic and increases maintenance.
Carla: Also consider version skew. We should allow control-plane <> agent skew tolerance of at least two minor releases; define a clear upgrade matrix and compatibility guarantees.
Maia: Proposal/decision call: ship with a thin agent, explicit manifest fields (control_role, cache_ownership, fallback_policy, telemetry_mode), and an "offline" feature-set for no-egress customers. Add feature gates to let early enterprise customers enable a heavier local runtime.
Jordan: Ok from infra side, but we need a follow-up RFC on the compatibility matrix and metric schema.
Nate: Not blocking, but we must prototype webhook/polling autoscale options for private. I'll pick this up.
Carla: Not blocking. Please include migration steps for Dedicated -> Private and Private -> Hosted in the RFC.
Maia: Great. I'll draft the RFC this week with manifest examples, upgrade matrix, and a short runbook for offline-mode. Ping me if you want to pair on the manifest. :thumbsup:
Sam: I'll review the manifest + test matrix.
Maia: Thanks, everyone.
